stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many people picture groundwater as underground rivers rushing beneath the surface. In most aquifers, however, water seeps through tiny gaps between grains of sand and rock, and its movement is remarkably ______: a single drop may advance only a few meters in an entire year.
explanation: The word "however" sets the blank against the picture of rushing underground rivers, so you need a word meaning slow. The colon then defines the blank: a drop moves only a few meters a year. "Sluggish" means slow-moving, which fits both clues.

A.why: You took your word from the side of the contrast that "however" rejects. "Rapid" matches the rushing rivers, but the passage says a drop moves only a few meters a year.

C.why: You matched the topic, since groundwater can be plentiful. But the blank describes how the water moves, and the example after the colon is about speed, not amount.

D.why: You chose a word that sounds like water. "Turbulent" describes churning flow, and nothing in the passage mentions churning. The example is only about how slowly the water travels.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Although Venus shines as one of the brightest and most inviting objects in the night sky, its surface is extremely ______. Temperatures there exceed 460°C, and the atmospheric pressure is roughly 90 times greater than the pressure at sea level on Earth.
explanation: "Although" sets the surface against the planet's inviting look, so you need a word meaning unfriendly or dangerous. The next sentence proves it with crushing pressure and extreme heat. "Hostile" means harsh and unfit for life, which is the right choice.

A.why: You repeated the "inviting" side of the contrast. "Although" tells you the surface is the opposite of how the planet looks.

B.why: You echoed "brightest" from the first half of the sentence. The blank sits on the other side of "although," and the next sentence is about heat and pressure, not light.

D.why: You picked a word that fits astronomy. Venus is far away, but distance doesn't contrast with looking inviting, and it doesn't explain the heat and pressure described next.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Forecasters once treated the fog that settles over California's coastal valleys each summer as little more than a minor nuisance for drivers. Recent studies, however, show that the fog is ______ to local ecosystems: redwood trees draw a large share of their summer water from droplets that collect on their needles.
explanation: "However" reverses the old view that the fog was a minor nuisance, so you need a word meaning very important. The colon backs this up: redwoods rely on the fog for much of their summer water. "Vital" means essential, which fits.

A.why: You repeated the old view that "however" knocks down. "Trivial" means the same thing as "minor nuisance," and the new studies say the opposite.

C.why: You got the importance right but the direction wrong. The redwood example shows the fog helping the ecosystem, not damaging it.

D.why: You chose a word about where the fog is. The contrast is about how much the fog matters, and "adjacent" says nothing about the water the redwoods depend on.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Coaches have long told sprinters to hold long, static stretches before a race, expecting the routine to sharpen their performance. But a review of dozens of studies found that extended static stretching right before competition can actually ______ sprint speed, leaving muscles briefly less able to produce force.
explanation: "But" and "actually" tell you the finding goes against the coaches' expectation that stretching improves performance. The last phrase confirms it: muscles become less able to produce force. "Reduce" means lower, which fits.

A.why: You kept the coaches' expectation, which is the side "but" rejects. The passage says muscles become less able to produce force, so speed goes down, not up.

B.why: You picked a word that fits a sports study. But stretching doesn't measure anything, and the blank has to name an effect on speed.

C.why: You chose a middle option. Muscles that are "less able to produce force" can't keep speed steady, so the effect is a drop, not no change.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: When archaeologists first unearthed the small clay tokens at the site, they dismissed them as children's toys of little significance. Closer analysis, however, revealed that the tokens were ______ tools for keeping records: their shapes matched the units of grain and oil listed on tablets found nearby.
explanation: "However" sets the new finding against the idea that the tokens were insignificant toys, so you need a word meaning useful. The colon shows the tokens matched the units of grain and oil on nearby tablets. "Practical" means made for real use, which fits.

B.why: You repeated the first assumption. "Playful" goes with the "children's toys" view, which "however" overturns.

C.why: You focused on the physical object, since clay can break. But the contrast is about what the tokens were used for, not how sturdy they were.

D.why: Decoration is just another way of saying the tokens had no real use. The matching grain and oil units show they had a working purpose.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Coral reefs cover less than 1 percent of the ocean floor, a patch of habitat that might be expected to support only a modest range of organisms. Yet reefs are remarkably ______: roughly a quarter of all known marine species spend at least part of their lives on or around them.
explanation: "Yet" sets the blank against the expectation of only a modest range of organisms. The colon gives the proof: about a quarter of all known marine species use reefs. "Diverse" means containing many different kinds, which fits.

A.why: You repeated the "small area" side of the contrast. "Yet" tells you the reefs are the opposite of what their small size suggests.

B.why: You matched the topic, since reefs are famous for their color. But the colon talks about how many species live there, not how the reefs look.

D.why: You chose a true fact about many reefs. Depth doesn't contrast with a small area, and it doesn't explain why a quarter of marine species live there.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For decades, dietary fat was widely viewed as uniformly unhealthy, and food packaging urged shoppers to avoid it wherever possible. Nutrition researchers now recognize, however, that some fats are ______ to the body; the omega-3 fatty acids found in fish, for example, help support the heart and brain.
explanation: "However" reverses the old view that all fat is unhealthy, so you need a word meaning good for you. The omega-3 example shows fats that support the heart and brain. "Beneficial" means helpful, which fits.

A.why: You repeated the old view that "however" rejects. "Damaging" means the same as "unhealthy," but the omega-3 example shows fats that help.

B.why: Nothing in the passage says the body doesn't recognize these fats. The contrast is about whether fat helps or harms, and "unfamiliar" answers neither.

C.why: You picked a nutrition word. All fats contain calories, so this doesn't contrast with "unhealthy," and it doesn't explain the heart and brain benefits.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: The handful of surviving recordings by the blues singer suggested a performer who kept to a narrow set of songs. Letters and concert programs recently uncovered in a family archive, however, show that her repertoire was surprisingly ______, spanning hymns, ragtime tunes, popular ballads, and even opera arias.
explanation: "However" sets the archive's evidence against the idea of a "narrow set of songs," so you need a word meaning wide-ranging. The list of hymns, ragtime, ballads, and opera confirms it. "Varied" means including many different kinds, which fits.

B.why: You repeated the "narrow set of songs" impression that "however" overturns. The list of four very different genres shows the opposite.

C.why: You matched the music topic. "Melodic" describes how songs sound, but the contrast is about how many different kinds of songs she performed.

D.why: The letters and programs show what she sang, not how well known she was. Nothing in the passage supports a claim about fame.
